title: Deuteronomy 31: Israel's future idolatry foretold to Moses
source_text: IV. Sic quoque Deuteronomii capite trigesimo primo Deus ad Mosen dixisse legitur, Ecce tu dormiturus es cum Patribus tuis: postea surget populus iste, & fornicabitur post Deos alienigenas terrae, ad quam pergit ut habitet in medio ejus; & derelinquet me, irritumque faciet pactum meum, quod pepigi cum eo. Quas praedictiones certas & infallibiles fuisse, eventus docuit illis per omnia respondens.
pass_a_gloss: Thus also in the thirty-first chapter of Deuteronomy God is read to have said to Moses, Behold thou shalt sleep with thy Fathers: afterward this people shall rise up, and go a whoring after the strange Gods of the land, whither it goes to dwell in the midst of it; and shall forsake me, and make void my covenant, which I made with it. Which predictions the event taught were certain and infallible, answering them in all things.
pass_b_english: Likewise in Deuteronomy 31 God is recorded as saying to Moses: 'You are about to sleep with your fathers. Then this people will rise up and prostitute themselves to the foreign gods of the land they are entering to live in. They will forsake me and break my covenant that I made with them.'
The outcome, matching these predictions in every respect, showed that they were certain and infallible.

choices.why: The standard English term for God's knowing in advance; 'foreknowledge' is kept throughout for praescientia, with 'foresee' for praevidere.
